criteria.criterion: Rust feasibility prototype of the PQXDH + Triple Ratchet/SPQR-class state machine runs on native and wasm32 with state persistence/reload
criteria.note: PQXDH rev3 + Triple Ratchet (EC DR + Signal spqr SCKA). 249 steps, each in a fresh process/instance, 367 messages incl. out-of-order and skipped keys carried across reloads, SPQR epoch 5; native, wasm32-wasip1 (wasmtime), alternating native/wasip1 and wasm32-unknown-unknown (Node/V8) produce byte-identical state at every step.

criteria.criterion: deterministic vectors produced by the prototype are consumed by a second independent implementation or checked against upstream KATs
criteria.note: Python (cryptography + kyber-py) reproduces 180/180 values over 16 messages (PQXDH, XEdDSA verify, ML-KEM, DR keys, KDF_HYBRID, headers, bit-exact AES-GCM-SIV ciphertexts) and rejects a mutated vector. NIST ACVP ML-KEM-768: 80/80 on libcrux (native+wasi), 80/80 on kyber-py. Scope limit: SPQR message keys are inputs (Signal's spqr is the only implementation). Same agent wrote both implementations (different language/libraries); see independence.

criteria.criterion: one-time key material handling and depletion behavior demonstrated without downgrade
criteria.note: 20 checks pass on native, wasip1 and Node: depletion to signed last-resort ML-KEM key, single-use deletion, replay rejection (one-time and last-resort), tampered handshake does not consume keys, PQ-less bundle / forged prekey / CT-less message / SPQR V0 all refused. Single provider pool only; multi-provider disjoint pools and multi-device (V-003) not exercised.

criteria.criterion: dependency, licensing and update strategy recorded in an ADR
criteria.note: Draft ADR written; needs an integrator to file it under decisions/ and an operator/legal decision on the AGPL-3.0-only spqr dependency vs the MPL-2.0 core policy.

criteria.criterion: no reliance on an unsupported external library API contract
criteria.note: libsignal (explicitly unsupported outside Signal) is not used. spqr is used only via its 3-function public API with OM-owned state/wire framing, but it has no crates.io release, no written external support statement and is AGPL-3.0-only; its wire message and state encodings are spqr-defined.

criteria.criterion: [pre-release] independent cryptographic review of the integrated production path
criteria.note: Needs an external reviewer; out of scope for an agent prototype.

criteria.criterion: [pre-release] production build provably excludes dev/test CryptoProvider (R-072)
criteria.note: Sketch only: `production` + `insecure-test-rng` is a compile_error!, the production build succeeds, and its compiled rlib contains no InsecureTestRng (the test build's does, as a control). A release-pipeline proof is still needed.

criteria.criterion: V-001 and V-005 prototypes record crypto and codec costs on native and wasm32 against the budgets; unattainable budgets revised by ADR
criteria.note: V-001 crypto costs recorded on native, wasm32-wasip1 (wasmtime) and wasm32-unknown-unknown (Node/V8); medians are far inside both budgets even with a 10x low-end factor. Measured on an Apple M3, not a reference low-end device; V-005 codec costs not covered here.

independence.authorship: written by a Claude agent; the design package was authored by a ChatGPT design agent and Claude agents; ADR-0117 (proposed) decides whether an AI reviewer counts as independent
limitations: both implementations written by the same AI agent in one session
no independent reimplementation of SPQR/ML-KEM Braid
independence.second_implementation: Python 3 (cryptography, kyber-py) written from the public specs; different language and different primitive libraries than the Rust side (dalek, libcrux, RustCrypto)
independence.upstream_code: SPQR is Signal's own implementation (spqr v1.6.0), not OM-authored
independence.upstream_kat: NIST ACVP-Server ML-KEM-768 internalProjection.json (keyGen, encapsulation, decapsulation, key checks) at a pinned commit with SHA-256

summary.upstream_probes: not run (use run.sh --long); last recorded results are in README.md
